strings.name: John Hennessy
strings.summary: John Hennessy led Stanford's MIPS reduced-instruction-set research and co-founded a company to turn architectural ideas into chips. He co-authored textbooks with David Patterson and shared the 2017 Turing Award. As Stanford president he supported interdisciplinary research and financial aid; after that tenure he worked on Knight-Hennessy Scholars and corporate governance, connecting computer engineering with higher education.

strings.facts.fact-2.value: Villanova electrical-engineering bachelor's (1973); Stony Brook computer-science master's (1975), PhD (1977)
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: MIPS and RISC
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Led Stanford's RISC research and co-founded MIPS to bring efficient architectures into industrial use.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Education and leadership
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Co-authored architecture textbooks with Patterson and promoted collaboration through university and graduate-program leadership.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Marconi lifetime award announced
strings.timeline.event-1.text: The Marconi Society named him its lifetime-achievement honoree for computing and educational contributions.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Shared Draper Prize
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Shared the engineering prize for contributions to RISC processors.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: 2017 Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Honored with David Patterson for methods of computer-architecture design and evaluation.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Presidency ended and scholars program
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Concluded his Stanford presidency and became inaugural director of Knight-Hennessy Scholars.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Became Stanford president
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Became Stanford's tenth president after serving as department chair, engineering dean and provost.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Co-founded Atheros
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Helped establish the wireless-chip company, extending his work into Wi-Fi technology.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Co-founded MIPS
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Established MIPS Computer Systems during a sabbatical to commercialize RISC technology.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Stanford RISC research
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Assembled a team to explore processor performance through reduced instruction sets.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Doctorate and Stanford faculty
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Completed his Stony Brook computer-science PhD and joined Stanford's faculty.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Villanova bachelor's degree
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Earned an electrical-engineering degree before computer-science graduate study at Stony Brook.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in New York state
